newsitem.title: FRANCE: ATHLETICS-MORCELI LEFT WITH MIXED FEELINGS IN NICE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-MORCELI LEFT WITH MIXED FEELINGS IN NICE.

text.p: Noureddine Morceli of Algeria was left with mixed feelings after seeing two of his world records survive at the Nice grand prix on Wednesday -- especially since he wanted to break one of them.

Morceli watched with satisfaction as Moroccan Hicham El Guerrouj clocked three minutes 30.32 seconds and failed to break the world 1,500 metres record of 3:27.37 seconds Morceli set on this track on a memorable night two years ago.
But the Algerian Olympic 1,500 metres champion then failed to derive much pleasure from his own attempt to beat his own world mile record of 3:44.39.
Morceli ran 3:48.64 -- only the fifth fastest time in the world this year -- and well outside the record he set in Rieti nearly four years ago.

Morceli, however, could gain some measure of satisfaction in the final grand prix meeting before next month's world championships in Athens with the emphatic style of his victory, finishing well clear of Kenyan Noah Ngeny (3:50.41) with France's Said Chebili a distant third in 3:52.21.
Morceli has looked out of sorts for most of the summer and, while not in the devastating form of recent years, he will still be in contention for gold in Athens. So, of course will El Guerrouj.

The Moroccan, who twice this month has gone close to breaking Morceli's world marks in both the 1,500 metres and mile, made it a hat-trick of near misses after being let down by some over-ambitious pacemaking by Kenyan Reuben Chesang and Vincent Malakwen.
But he still clocked the second fastest time of the year and only he has run quicker.

El Guerrouj was left to cover the last lap in around 53 seconds after going through the bell at 2:34 and could manage only 56 seconds. He actually went closer to the record in Stockholm last week when he ran 3:29.30, the fastest in the world this year.
However, he was pushed all the way to the line by Kenyan John Kibowen, who finished second in 3:30.44 with Kenyan William Tanui, the 1992 800 metres Olympic champion, third in 3:31.62.
Kibowen, little-known before the start of this season, has run some impressive times this summer, but this race served notice he could be a real threat to the more established names very soon.
Maksim Tarasov of Russia, the 1992 Olympic champion, had a night to remember when he became only the fifth man in history to clear 6.00 metres in the pole vault.

He won a high-calibre competition which included France's Olympic champion Jean Galfione, with a clearance of 6.00 metres to join Sergei Bubka (6.15), South African Okkert Brits (6.03), Radion Gataullin (6.02) and Igor Trandenkov (6.01) in that event's role of honour.
Portuguese women Fernanda Ribeiro and Carla Sacramento both ran the fastest times of the year in their respective events -- the 3,000 metres and mile.

Ribeiro, the Olympic 10,000 champion, proved she is coming into form at the right time by running a year's best eight minutes 37.14 seconds in the 3,000, while Sacramento won a closely fought mile race in 4:25.00.
South African teenager Llewellyn Herbert, who finished with a silver medal in the world junior championships last year, was another impressive winner in the 400 metres hurdles.
He outpaced Zambia's Olympic silver medalist Samuel Matete over the last two hurdles to win in 48.17 seconds with Matete second in 48.37.

European champion Geir Moen of Norway finished his preparations for the world championships with a win in the 200 metres, but had to find some extra speed in the last 30 metres to overtake 19-year-old Seun Ogunkoya of Nigeria.
The African 100 champion, who led from the start but wilted over the last few strides.

"I am really tired now after running a lot recently," said Moen, "and I have to be ready for the worlds. It's going to be tough. Ato Boldon is in great shape so is Frankie Fredericks and Maurice Greene -- and Michael Johnson hasn't even started running yet."
Moen clocked 20.41, with American Rohsaan Griffin second in 20.50, the same time as Ogunkoya, who was placed third.

Jamaican Merlene Ottey, who at 37 will be attempting to retain her world 200 title next month, appeared to be in fine form winning her race in 22.47 seconds, her best of the summer, ahead of compatriot Juliet Campbell (22.61).

Ottey, who first competed in a major championship before some of today's younger athletes started eating solids, said: "It's probably my last chance of another title. But I feel fine and will be going for it again in Athens."

Other winners included American Kim Batten in the 400 metres hurdles (53.71), Astrid Kumbernuss in the women's shot (20.51 metres) and Sarka Kasparkova of the Czech Republic in the women's triple jump (14.72 metres), Anier Garcia of Cuba in the men's 110 hurdles (13.18) and Melissa Morrison (12.63) in the women's 100 hurdles.
